attempts.raw_response: The 32-year-old from Manchester was diagnosed with a severe brain infection that left her fighting for her life. Her husband Mark, who works as a electrician, has been at her bedside every day since she was admitted to Salford Royal Hospital. "We don't know when she'll wake up," he said. "The doctors say it's a waiting game now." Friends and family launched the online fundraiser to help with medical costs and to support the family during her recovery. "Tracy was so looking forward to the marathon - she'd been training for months," said her sister Lisa. "She was doing it for charity. That's just who she is." The campaign has now gone viral, with messages of support flooding in from across the globe. Doctors say it's too early to say what the long-term effects might be.

pair.human_continuation: She was treated for meningitis, septicaemia, blood clots and bleeding on the brain, her sister-in-law said. Doctors had to amputate her feet and legs below the knee, as well as her fingers. She has been in intensive care at St Thomas' Hospital in London, but might soon be moved back to Southend Hospital for further treatment, Mrs Ralph said. "We decided to start fundraising because we want to give Tracy what she needs," said Mrs Ralph. "The house will need to be renovated, she'll need prosthetics, an adapted car, a wheelchair, support from carers - we have no idea how much that's going to cost. "If the money's there that people have so kindly donated, at least she'll have options," Mrs Ralph added.
pair.prefix: Almost £80,000 of a £100,000 target has been raised in four days. "It's a miracle. There must be a higher power at work here," Mrs Ralph told the BBC. "We've had contributions from all over world, people have been giving thousands of pounds. We appreciate every penny." Intensive care Tracy, a mother of two small boys, was planning on running a half marathon later this year, but had to be put into an induced coma on Christmas Day.

source_document.title: 'Astonishing' donations for leg amputee mum Tracy Ralph
